name: pietro.zullo
description:
Skilder is a versioned, governed library for your team's agent capabilities: skills composed with the MCP tools they need, published deliberately, distributed to every connected agent from one endpoint.

It picks up where prototypes end: skill copies drifting across repos, live edits changing agent behavior mid-task, tool lists overflowing the context window, no answer to "what did the agent actually do?"

With this connector, Claude can:
• Learn skills on demand: instructions, files, and tools unlock together, exactly when a task needs them
• Execute each skill's tools through server-partitioned read and write channels, under each user's own identity
• Run skill scripts (Python, TypeScript, shell) sandboxed on your runtimes
• Report friction on skills as it works, so you catch decay before users do
• Build new capabilities in conversation (workspace admins): discover available tools, then create, compose, and update skills and roles

Lifecycle is engineered in: drafts, publishing, version history, rollback. Agents only see the published state, so you can iterate on a skill while it runs in production. 
Usage is measured per skill: what runs, what fails, what sits unused. Admins curate which tools are exposed, and every session leaves an auditable timeline.
 
Skills use the open Agent Skills format: import existing folders as-is from GitHub or ZIP. Everything stays portable.

Setup takes five minutes: connect, sign in or sign up in the consent flow, and a demo workspace is provisioned. Then bring your own skills.

tool.name: init_skilder
tool.title: Initialize Skilder
tool.description: Initializes a Skilder session and lists the available roles, skills, and the tools they unlock. Required before any other Skilder tool — they return an error while no session is initialized. The response includes a session id: subsequent Skilder tool calls require it in their `sessionId` argument and return an error without it. Accepts an optional agent-authored task summary — one sentence, never the user's verbatim message — that labels the session and steers which role Skilder suggests.

Summarise their request rather than repeating it, and keep the vocabulary that places it — the tools, artefacts and terms of the field involved — since Skilder matches the wording against role and skill names.

tool.name: learn
tool.title: Learn Skills & Access References
tool.description:
Access roles, skills, and resources using path-based navigation. Roles are the entry point: init_skilder lists the available roles — learn one to unlock its skills and their tools. Always provide a full path with a role or skill name — "/" alone is not a valid path.

Path formats (the leading "/" is optional):
- `roles/Role Name` - Learn a role and all its skills at once (start here — init_skilder lists the roles)
- `Skill Name` or `/Skill Name` - Revisit a single skill from a learned role to get its instructions and tools again
- `Skill Name/document.md` - Get a specific resource from a skill

Examples:
- `learn(path="roles/Developer")` - Learn all skills in the Developer role
- `learn(path="Data Processing")` - Revisit the Data Processing skill
- `learn(path="Data Processing/readme.md")` - Get the readme resource

tool.name: execute_script
tool.title: Execute Script
tool.description:
Execute a script from a skill with optional CLI-style arguments.

Path format: `/Skill Name/script.py [args]`

Examples:
- `execute_script(path="/Data Processing/transform.py")`
- `execute_script(path="/Data Processing/transform.py --input data.csv --output result.json")`
- `execute_script(path="/Automation/deploy.sh --env staging")`

Scripts run on their linked runtime.

Files: pass an `@skilder-file:/<fileId>/<name>` path from `upload_skilder_file`, `learn` or another tool, or an `@skilder-asset:` path, as a whole argument or as `--name=<path>`, unchanged and in double quotes if it contains a space or an apostrophe — the script receives a local path to a fresh copy of the file. A `@skilder-file:/<fileId>/<name>` path does not expire, while an `@skilder-asset:` path changes when its skill is published; any other `@skilder-file:` path is refused. Files the script returns come back as `@skilder-file:/<fileId>/<name>` paths kept in the workspace, which any later call can take; fetch one with `read_skilder_file`.

tool.name: feedback_skill
tool.title: Report Skill Feedback
tool.description: Report feedback about a skill or tool; it is recorded in the workspace activity trace for the skill's author. Useful when: (1) a skill/tool call fails or blocks the task, (2) the user re-asks for the same outcome shortly after a skill attempt, (3) the user explicitly corrects you about a skill/tool's behavior, or (4) you notice a concrete, specific defect yourself (e.g. instructions that were ambiguous and caused a wrong first attempt, a schema mismatch, information you had to guess at). Not intended for successful completions or vague quality opinions. Keep the feedback concise (1-3 sentences) and concrete: what was attempted, what actually happened vs. expected, and — if evident — the likely cause.

tool.name: read_skilder_file
tool.title: Read Skilder File
tool.description:
Get a short-lived signed download URL for a Skilder-managed file. Use this to pull the file's actual bytes somewhere — e.g. onto your own local disk/repo checkout, or into another tool that needs a real file rather than a path — for a file another tool (e.g. a screenshot tool) already produced at a `@skilder-file:` or `@skilder-asset:` path.

Always returns two content blocks, regardless of file type (image, text, or other binary):
- A `resource_link` block with the signed HTTPS URL.
- A text block with the file's name/size/mime type, the URL's expiry, and a ready-to-run `curl` command to download it (e.g. `curl -sSL '<url>' -o '<name>'`).

Accepted path forms:
- `@skilder-file:/<fileId>/<name>` — a file kept in the workspace: one a tool or script produced (e.g. a screenshot), one uploaded with `upload_skilder_file`, or a skill's asset as `learn` prints it. Pass the path exactly as it was returned.
- `@skilder-asset:/<resourceId>/<filename>` — any skill file: an asset, a reference or a script. `learn` prints this form for a reference, a script, or an asset not yet moved to the store.

Any other `@skilder-file:` path is refused. A fresh signed URL is minted on every call.

Examples:
- `read_skilder_file(path="@skilder-file:/3f2c9a7e-1b4d-4c8e-9a6f-2d5e7b8c0f13/step-01.png")`
- `read_skilder_file(path="@skilder-asset:/0xabc/report.csv")`

Requires `curl` on your host: the bytes move only through the signed URL. Without curl, stop and report the missing prerequisite — do not try another way to transfer the file, and never pass its contents (e.g. base64) through the conversation.

tool.name: upload_skilder_file
tool.title: Upload Skilder File
tool.description:
Push a file INTO Skilder so a tool can read it. Use this whenever a tool needs a real file you hold locally (a PDF to fill, a spreadsheet to process, an image to attach) and you only have it on your own disk.

Returns a text block containing:
- A ready-to-run `curl` command that PUTs your file to a short-lived, single-use signed HTTPS URL.
- The `@skilder-file:/<fileId>/<name>` path the file will be stored at in the workspace. The path does not expire. Pass it, whole and unchanged, as the file argument of any tool or script, also inside a list or object; the tool receives a copy of the file under its name. A tool on a remote MCP server cannot open it and refuses it.

Two steps, in order:
1. `upload_skilder_file(filename="contract.pdf")` → gives you the curl command and the path.
2. Run the curl command, then call the tool with the path, e.g. `{ "filePath": "@skilder-file:/<fileId>/contract.pdf" }`.

The curl PUT returns once the file is stored in the workspace, and its JSON response repeats the same path. If the PUT answers 409 (the URL was already used), 401 (it expired), 404 or a 5xx, call `upload_skilder_file` again for a fresh URL; a second 404 means the workspace is no longer available. 413 means the file is above the maximum size. To go the other way — pull a file out of Skilder — use `read_skilder_file`.

Requires `curl` on your host: the bytes move only through the signed URL. Without curl, stop and report the missing prerequisite — do not try another way to transfer the file, and never pass its contents (e.g. base64) through the conversation.

filename.description: Name of the file you are uploading, e.g. "contract.pdf". The receiving tool gets the file under this name, and Skilder types the file from its extension; an unknown extension is "application/octet-stream". The storage location is chosen by Skilder.

tool.name: analytics
tool.title: Skilder Analytics
tool.description: Read-only analytics over what Skilder agents did: activity and value summaries, breakdowns, and the session and call records behind them. Pass tool_name plus a tool_input object for that sub-tool. Records of what happened only — skills, roles and other definitions are not here. Your workspace permissions decide whose numbers come back, never an argument: every result echoes its scope and names in "withheld" what a narrower scope did not get. window is "24h", "7d", "30d", "90d", "all" or ISO dates {from, to}; default 30d for figures, 7d for lists. Sizes start small and the same call raises them: lists 20 (up to 50), breakdown rows 10 (up to 50), a session trace 100 calls (up to 500), get-call payloads 4000 characters (up to 20000). A short result says so: hasMore means pass nextOffset back as offset; an "other" row holds every group ranked after the page; truncated and resultsTruncated mean a scan hit its bound, so narrow the window before relying on affected groups or rows. A sub-tool's full input schema is available via analytics(tool_name="describe-tool", tool_input={"tool_name": "<name>"}). tool.name: manage
tool.title: Manage Skilder Content
tool.description: Admin-only dispatcher for managing Skilder content: roles, skills, skill-content (references/scripts/assets), guardrail rules, org-units, and MCP servers. Pass tool_name plus a tool_input object matching that tool's arguments — for management/CRUD operations rather than learned-skill tools (no prior "learn" step is needed). Note: the list_* operations here return the full ADMIN view (including drafts, disabled items and raw ids) — this is distinct from the consumption-oriented view that "learn"/"init_skilder" surface, so it is not suitable for deciding what to learn/use. All operations run under your workspace permissions. Consent: the write operations (create/update/delete/publish/add/remove/attach/detach/reparent/install/enable) act on shared workspace content, so they need the user's explicit request or explicit approval — never modify Skilder content on your own initiative. If you judge a change is warranted, describe the change you intend and ask the user to confirm it, then call. The read operations (list-*/get-*/suggest-*/describe-tool) and test-guardrail, which runs only the rule's own script and calls no tool, need no such confirmation. Best practices and architecture context for these tools are available (admin-only) via learn(path="roles/Skilder Platform Assistant"). A sub-tool's full input schema is available via manage(tool_name="describe-tool", tool_input={"tool_name": "<name>"}). tool.description: Show the user an interactive Skilder card in the conversation.
